title: SCOUT 2.0 ROBOT
description:
SCOUT 2.0 is AgileX’s all‑round outdoor mobile research platform built for unstructured field environments. Equipped with a four‑wheel independent double‑wishbone suspension and 115 mm ground clearance, it delivers off‑road mobility, stably travelling across sand, gravel, slopes and bumpy ground while protecting onboard payloads.

Powered by four 400 W servo motors and swappable lithium‑iron‑phosphate battery packs, it supports dual‑battery configurations for flexible range from 15 km to 30 km. It sustains 2.5‑hour continuous operation under full load, ideal for long‑duration field deployments.

Boasting an open expansion architecture, the chassis offers a 24 V 10 A external power supply and abundant mounting interfaces. Users can integrate LiDAR, RTK‑INS, robotic arms and auto‑charging modules effortlessly. It fits diverse use‑cases including field exploration, industrial inspection prototypes, unmanned patrols and agricultural monitoring.

Designed for research and industrial prototyping, SCOUT 2.0 provides a robust hardware foundation for autonomous driving and outdoor robotics development. *3D renders for reference only, subject to physical product.*

title: Trace 2.0 Robot - Indoor Handling Mobile Development Platform
description:
# TRACER 2.0 | AgileX Indoor Mobile Development Platform

The TRACER 2.0 is AgileX’s upgraded differential-drive mobile chassis, built to deliver dependable, high-performance mobility for indoor logistics, industrial transport and academic research. Designed for developers and enterprises seeking a robust off-the-shelf robotic base, it balances heavy-load capacity, environmental adaptability and convenient integration to streamline robot deployment and secondary development.

Built with a modular framework, TRACER 2.0 operates reliably across challenging indoor working conditions. It carries an IP22 ingress protection rating and supports a wide operating temperature range from -10°C to 40°C. The chassis can traverse obstacles up to 10 mm high and cross trenches as wide as 30 mm, enabling steady travel on uneven factory floors, lab spaces and mixed indoor sites without frequent modification.

A redesigned three-swing-arm structure forms the core mechanical upgrade. This innovation effectively reduces chassis deformation under full load, preserving precise motion tracking even at the rated payload of 150 kg. With a curb weight between 54 kg and 56 kg, the platform maintains outstanding stability during acceleration, turning and stopping, backed by servo braking that achieves a short stopping distance of just 0.8 m under standard test conditions.

Power performance has been comprehensively enhanced. It is equipped with two 400 W servo motors and a high-capacity 24 V, 30 Ah lithium iron phosphate battery. The platform reaches a top speed of 2 m/s with no load, offering up to 70 km of travel range when empty and 25 km at full load. The battery features a bottom quick-release mechanism, cutting down swap time and supporting continuous high-intensity workflows. It also supplies 24 V, 15 A external power output to carry onboard sensors, computing units and auxiliary modules.
